clues: This city lies at the head of a bay on the central coast of Honshu. Honshu is the largest island in this island nation.
Summers here are hot and damp, and winters are cool with cold spells at times. Sea storms called typhoons reach this coast in most years.
In 1603, the Tokugawa rulers made this city their seat of power. It grew from a small fishing village into a vast city.
An old castle stands at the heart of this city, and the emperor lives in its grounds today. It became his palace when the court moved here in 1868.
The emperor and the government of Japan sit in this city. Its law makers meet here in the Diet hall.
